lesson.planet_with_rings.title: Planet With Rings
lesson.planet_with_rings.summary: Build a centered planet, make its rings pass behind and in front, then invent the world’s own surface, moons and mood.
lesson.planet_with_rings.step.planet_bod: Start with one large planet shape near the center. Aim for a confident round form, not a perfect circle.
lesson.planet_with_rings.help.planet_bod: Leave breathing room around the planet so its rings will have space to travel.
lesson.planet_with_rings.complete.planet: The planet has a clear centered mass.
lesson.planet_with_rings.step.ring_overl: Draw the ring as two broad arcs. One travels behind the planet and the other comes across the front.
lesson.planet_with_rings.help.ring_overl: Think behind first, then front. The overlap is what makes the ring feel wrapped around the planet.
lesson.planet_with_rings.complete.ring_o: The ring now reads as something circling the planet.
lesson.planet_with_rings.step.moons_surf: Add a moon and a few broad surface marks. Keep them simple enough that the planet shape still reads first.
lesson.planet_with_rings.help.moons_surf: Place details where they support the big shape instead of filling every empty space.
lesson.planet_with_rings.complete.moons_: A few details now suggest a larger world.
lesson.planet_with_rings.step.design: Now invent your planet. Change the ring thickness, surface patterns, moon count or the color mood—these are choices, not answers.
lesson.planet_with_rings.help.design: Choose one idea that makes this planet feel different from the teacher example.
lesson.planet_with_rings.complete.drawin: Your planet has its own rings, details and mood.
